newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two bidders for Mexico's NE railway likely exempt.
newsitem.headline: Two bidders for Mexico's NE railway likely exempt.

text.p: Two bidders for Mexico's Northeast Railway will probably be disqualified from bidding to operate the key trade route because they are not majority owned by a Mexican company, sources at the Communications and Transport ministry told Reuters on Tuesday.

Illinois Central Corp and the consortium led by French company GEC-Alsthom have not yet been excluded from bidding for the route's operations, scheduled to be decided on Thursday, but almost certainly will be, ministry sources said.

"Although they are not officially removed from the bidding process, the companies that do not fulfill the official requirements are very unlikely to be considered," said a ministry source who asked not to be identified.
Ministry sources said the two companies did not fulfill the required 51 percent ownership by a Mexican company.

The government is selling off an 80 percent share with 20 percent to be floated on the Mexican Stock Exchange within the next two years. GEC-Alsthom representatives were not available for comment Tuesday.
An Illinois Central spokeswoman said the company was in talks with potential Mexican partners, but would not provide further details.

"We are very interested in the entire privatisation process," said Ann Thoma, spokeswoman with Illinois Central in Chicago. "Our area of greatest interest is in the southeast (of Mexico). We have to approach Mexico from a different angle to determine our investment niche."
Illinois Central operates two rail systems, one from Chicago south to the state of Louisiana and the other from Chicago west through the state of Iowa.
The Mexican government commonly requires that bidders in privatisations be majority Mexican owned. Ministry officials said rules in the bidding for the Northeast rail were not likely to change.
Mexican companies and consortia led by Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM), Empresas ICA and Grupo Mexico are expected to be key competitors in operating the railway.

On Thursday the ministry will review prices offered for the railway and announce the winning bid. Only bids above the estimate from an independent assessor will be considered, and the sale will be declared null if no offers register above the estimate.
